dx_raw:
DIAGNOPRESENTATION: GCH1-related dopa-responsive dystonia (Segawa syndrome)

The genetic testing has provided the definitive diagnosis. Dopa-responsive dystonia typically presents in childhood or adolescence, often with diurnal fluctuation of symptoms (worse in the evening, better after sleep). The gait may show subtle dystonic posturing, reduced arm swing, or stiffness that can be intermittent and easily missed on a routine examination—which explains why the formal neurological exam was otherwise normal. Many patients are misdiagnosed with cerebral palsy or functional neurological disorder before the correct diagnosis is made.

Alternative diagnoses to consider:

1. Early Parkinson's disease with atypical or subtle presentation
2. Dystonia-parkinsonism spectrum disorder (other genetic causes)
3. Functional neurological disorder (gait disturbance)
